content:
maya.sre: heads-up — customer report: p95/p99 spikes for embeddings API in us-west after yesterday's driver + GPU FW roll. opening triage thread. saw ~3x p99 at ingestion path.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-10T22:10:34 -> drivers/gpu-driver-525.8 + fw 2.4.7 rolled to us-west-1 at 22:12 UTC (canary -> 30% -> 100%).

eli.eng: thanks. links to the SLO chart? which routes impacted (generate vs embed)?

maya.sre: embed route mostly, small-batch latency shows p95 ~200ms -> 800ms, p99 up to 1.6s. generate unaffected.

liv-cs: customer "AcmeAds" reporting timeouts and increased retries, provided sample request ids: r_20260310_118234, r_20260310_118875. they saw spike start ~22:20 UTC.

ej: iowait/host-io looks suspicious in earlier incidents — can we get iostat/journal output from impacted nodes?

jordan-plat: run these on a repro node:
```
iostat -x 1 5
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE
cat /proc/interrupts | grep nvme
kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --tail=200
```

maya.sre: pasted trimmed iostat from node ip-10-0-12-71 (22:25 UTC):
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.50   44.30  1024.0  8192.0    0.00   12.00  45.60  6.20  52.40  0.80  98.40
```

maya.sre: %util ~98 and await high -> clear host I/O saturation. saw KV-cache eviction spikes coincident with this (cache hit drops).

eli.eng: KV cache thrash could amplify latency. did driver FW change NVMe queue handling? vendor notes mention firmware IO scheduling tweak in 2.4.7.

jordan-plat: check kernel logs for blk-mq/backpressure: `dmesg | grep -i blk` and nvme timeouts. also `cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/io_scheduler` for scheduler.

maya.sre: kernel shows repeated "nvme0: I/O 0x... timed out" messages every ~30s after 22:18, and blk_mq warnings.

liv-cs: customer is asking for ETA and mitigation, they're hitting production traffic.

ej: quick mitigation options: 1) route customer to unaffected region, 2) limit background batch jobs on those hosts, 3) throttle write-heavy tasks, 4) roll back driver/fw. which is fastest?

jordan-plat: routing is fastest if we have capacity. rollback is riskier but likely to eliminate regression. intermediate: reduce per-node concurrent embeddings workers (env var EMBED_CONCURRENCY=6) and enable aggressive KV cache warmup to avoid evictions.

maya.sre: tried lowering concurrency on two canary nodes, p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 720ms within 90s. good sign.

ops-bot: NOTE: action_required -> schedule rollback window? Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/host-io-spike

eli.eng: let's collect perf traces before rollback. run `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` and capture iostat, nvme logs. also grab pod profiles: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- pstack $(pidof server)` if possible.

maya.sre: collecting traces now, will attach to ticket. also capturing host-level cgroup blkio stats and `echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` not recommended on prod but used on a repro host — saw small improvement in kv hit recovery.

jordan-plat: low-risk mitigations we'll apply immediately: - set EMBED_CONCURRENCY=6 via config override on us-west service pool, - add blkio.weight=500 to cgroup for infra writers, - temporarily divert non-critical batch loads.

liv-cs: messaging to customer: "We identified host storage contention correlated with the recent GPU driver/firmware rollout. We're applying throttles and routing changes now and preparing a rollback if stability doesn't improve. We'll update in 30m."

eli.eng: if rollback needed, coordinate with infra team — rollback plan: drivers/gpu-driver-524.x + fw 2.4.3, take nodes out of rotation, apply, validate with 10% canary, then 100% if ok. estimate 45-60m.

maya.sre: agreed. current status: mitigations applied to 6 nodes, p99 down ~55% on those nodes. collecting traces to confirm root cause. will update thread with perf tarball link and decision in 20m. :thumbsup:
